utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, let's -- let's focus on the questions I'm asking you. Was General Pavkovic introduced or was it mentioned that he was speaking on behalf of the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this is not a black or white situation. You have to explain things. If he had spoken on behalf of the Joint Command, then he would have included all the components of all the structures that were present there, the army, the police, and he would brief on everything that was done in Kosovo. On that occasion and on previous meetings, he always --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I take it that your answer is you do not recall that? That's all I want to know. We're wasting time now. All the question asked is whether or not you recall whether what is recorded here is correct, that General Pavkovic spoke on behalf of the Joint Command. Can we have your answer so we could move on?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that he spoke on behalf of the Pristina Corps, and the head of the MUP staff spoke on behalf of the MUP forces that were engaged down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move on to page 3 in the English and also in the B/C/S. You see at the bottom there in referring to the outcome of the implementation of the plan, he said: "The following tasks were set in the said plan. "Taking measures to reinforce the security of the state border in the border belt and in depth. "Organising, equipping, and co-ordinating the operations of the MUP and VJ forces to oppose terrorist forces more successfully. "Taking control of territory in Kosovo and Metohija by MUP and VJ forces, and the establishment of conditions to unblock roads and occupied territory" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel is kindly asked to slow down when reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall that you reported on those tasks, among others?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not present any reports at those meetings and nobody ever asked me anything. But I remember that Pavkovic presented briefings on the implementation of the global plan for anti-terrorist activities which he himself drafted. And now when actions according to that plan were completed, he spoke about the implementation of the plan, the plan that he had presented at the first meeting on the 21st of July. So now he is saying what was done in accordance with this general plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page you see number 4 is: "Arming the Serbian and Montenegrin people and establishing reserve police units to defend Serbian villages." You recall that that was a part of the plan?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that it was an integral part of the plan --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall that --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- well, if you mean the establishment of the reserve police squads, well, I don't recall that being part of the plan. I remember the activities that related to that, but I don't recall whether it was or was not a part of the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could move to page 7 in both.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You spoke of General Lukic, who also made a contribution at this meeting. You even see here it is recorded by Lieutenant-General Curcic: "Major-General Sreten Lukic submitted a report on the work of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija, devoting special attention to the higher professional successful co-operation between the army and the police commands and units in performing the following tasks ..." Can you recall General Lukic making a presentation on the work of what is recorded here as the Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to say once again, you have to take into account what the note-taker is saying about the co-operation between the units of the army and the police, but he's using the term "milicija." At that time "milicija" was not the term that was used; it didn't exist. So this is just a free interpretation on the part of whoever was taking the notes and the minutes --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "Milicija" --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- all the terms that he's using here --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please stop, please stop, please stop. Please just focus on the question. Joint Command, that is the question or the part I want you to focus on says: "Major-General Lukic submitted a report on the work of the Joint Command ..." Is that your memory of General Lukic's presentation?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember quite clearly that he submitted a report, but he did not submit a report on the engagement of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija. This is a free interpretation of whoever drafted the minutes. Sreten Lukic submitted the report at the meeting on the topics that are listed here, the participation of the police in the implementation of the plan and the engagement in the previous period.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's go to page 9 in English, page 10 in B/C/S. Without going through the entire document, can I remind you or is it your memory that Mr. Milomir Minic also made a presentation at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And we see in conclusion he said: "The operations staff should provide an assessment of how successfully the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija has fulfilled the authorisations conferred upon it." Do you recall him saying that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after ten years I really can't say. I remember that he took part in the discussion, but now as to what he dealt with in his intervention and what his proposals were -- with the best of intentions I can't tell you whether he really did intervene in those terms as he is recorded here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's look at page 12 in English and the B/C/S. And you want to go to the bottom of page 12 in the Serbian version and the third -- fourth paragraph of page 12 in the English version. Surely, Mr. Djordjevic, you would remember what the president of the country said. This recalls the President of the Republic of Serbia, Milan Milutinovic, as considering that the reports submitted by the members of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija should be accepted. Do you recall that Mr. Milutinovic said that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how could I remember that after ten years? But I don't doubt that he actually said that, but I can't really remember it because I didn't take notes and after ten years it's really impossible for me to say what Milan Milutinovic said. I remember that Perisic intervened. I remember that all of those people did say something, but I can't really say now what is it that they said and whether he really did intervene on the issues that we see here in the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, this is the president talking about a group of people that you were a part of.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me if I remember, if I recall. You will admit that ten years is a long time. It's too long time for me to be able to remember every sentence that he uttered. It's likely that he did say everything that is recorded here, but at this point in time I can't remember whether he did or did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you look at the top of page 13 - if we could move to that in B/C/S and stay on the same page in English, please - we have the president of the country saying -- or the president of the country being reported as supporting the proposal for consideration of the continued status of the Joint Command. "Milutinovic believes that the Joint Command should continue functioning for a while, although thought should be given as to whether it should continue in its present membership or whether some changes should be made." Again, the president is commenting on a body that you were a part of and he is proposing that the body continue to operate. Do you remember him saying that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't doubt that he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we look at page 13 in English and it's also page 13 in B/C/S, the bottom of page 13 in B/C/S, we see the intervention of Deputy Prime Minister Sainovic. Do you remember that Deputy Prime Minister Sainovic also participated, he had comments to make at this meeting, do you?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As in the case of other participants in the discussion, I remember that they did say something; but now as to what they were saying and what the topic was, I really can't now say. Because I didn't take notes, I didn't produce any kind of aide-memoire --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and I don't doubt the record, the minutes, that really he did say what is recorded here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That the -- that he agreed with the continued activity of the Joint Command. That's what he says here. Is that what you have read?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find the place in the text, but I don't doubt the fact that it was -- it may have been debated too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The text here says at the bottom last two lines in your Serbian version: "Deputy Prime Minister" --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- I think it's that it there --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- scroll -- well, you can't see it. "The Vice-President Sainovic agreed with the opinion to consider the -- whether it is appropriate" -- well, he says that the number of people should be reduced and that they should be better prepared for more effective action in new conditions. This is what it says here. I suppose that the new conditions actually mean the agreements that were signed following the mediation of the international community in the crisis down there, and now it is quite natural that the engagement of the forces of both the army and the MUP should be adjusted to the new conditions. This is how I interpret it now that I'm reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Well, let's move to page 14 in English and page 15 in Serbian. This section I feel -- quite sure that you won't fail to remember this because this is President Milosevic himself speaking. "President Milosevic recommended to the president of the Republic of Serbia, Milan Milutinovic, to personally go to Kosovo and Metohija and explain the substance of the agreement which we have reached with the representatives of the international community to the presidents of districts and municipalities." And if we move to page 15 in the English and this is the same page at the bottom of page 15 in the B/C/S, so the B/C/S page should remain the same. Continuing his speech, President Milosevic in the third paragraph from top in the English version: "Continuing his speech, President Milosevic pointed to the need for the continuing function of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija ..." This is President Milosevic speaking about a body that you were a part of. Do you recall that he said this?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would be only too glad to be able to tell you that I remember it, but I don't. I don't doubt that he actually did say that. And then he says some kind of a co-ordination staff. I don't know now. The Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija and the co-ordination staff, I don't know what this co-ordination staff is. And I said that the title of this document is minutes from the meeting of the operational staff. Now all of a sudden there is this co-ordination staff. I really, in light of all the terms that are used here by the man who signed the minutes, I can't -- well, co-ordination staff and President Milosevic is supposed to have said that. This is the first time that I hear about co-ordination staff. I know that the state commission for the co-ordination of the activities with the OSCE was established and that it was chaired by Nikola Sainovic, and I know that Milan Milutinovic was ordered to go to Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that he went there and so was I --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, I'm sorry, you're going way beyond now what I was asking you about, and I wasn't really focusing on the title of the document, just the contents. You know, sometimes the title may be a matter of an administrative filing system. It's the contents. Just before we move from this document, can I ask you did you know Lieutenant-General -- I'm sure I'm going to get the pronunciation wrong, but I think you mentioned the name before - but Lieutenant-General Slavoljub Susic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know a Curcin but there might be a Curcic too. I know the name and I may know the man by sight but that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's look at the remainder of the document. You know the person who signed as having compiled these minutes?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that and I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who was --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the head of the military office of the president of the FRY. But I would like to ask you to show me when the minutes were actually drafted --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That was on the front page --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- the minutes are dated the 2nd of November. Can we move on to another document, P770. You can take my word for it, Mr. Djordjevic, they are dated the 2nd of November, but we have to move on quickly. P770, please.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see that. Yes, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These are the minutes of a MUP staff meeting of the 5th of November, 1998. You will recall I showed you from the notes of the previous meeting on the 29th of October, President Milosevic recommended that President Milutinovic should go to Kosovo and explain to the senior people there the way the country would proceed in the future, to explain what had been agreed and what would be done. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And this meeting, I think that's where you have it there in B/C/S, these minutes, the 5th of November, minutes held at the MUP staff in Pristina on the 5th of November. The meeting was attended by President Milutinovic; Minister of Interior Stojiljkovic; Colonel-General Djordjevic, chief of the public security department; Lieutenant-General Markovic; various other MUP generals and senior persons. It says: Staff member Nikola Sainovic and Milomir Minic, Zoran Andjelkovic, all of the major actors in Kosovo being present, General Pavkovic as well from the VJ, and the SUP chiefs, the special unit commanders are present. Now, you were asked about this document by counsel for Defence, and you said that this was Mr. Milutinovic down there supporting the people in Kosovo, it was a show of support. Be that as it may, I wanted to ask about one part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 2 of this presentation. And it's page 2 in English as well -- or the next page in English. At the top, about five or six lines from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The president, now in Kosovo, says: "With regard to the Yugoslav Army and the police, everything will stay the same as it has been up to now, (a Joint Command, VJ army units will not withdraw, and the police forces have only been reduced by the number that has already been withdrawn)." You remember the president, President Milutinovic, saying that the Joint Command would remain?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't doubt the words as they are written here. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But do you recall it? I ask you because I think it's important because you are recorded as having been at these meetings all through the offensive. These meetings involve massive use of force and massive, massive, police/army operations. It certainly must have been important in your career. They occupied you for the better part of one year, and the president is saying that this body should continue. That's why I keep asking you if you remember him saying that. Do you remember him saying that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right now I do not remember, but I do not doubt that he uttered those words. I can't tell you that I remember when I don't remember whether he said "Joint Command" or as is written here remains, the army units are not being withdrawn and police forces are being reduced, and so on. They had to act in accordance with the agreements that had been signed. Had we not done it, we would have been bombed again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Right. That, again, is interesting but not on point. Back to the Joint Command which is the point I want to focus on. You will agree with me, having said you don't doubt that he used these terms that are recorded in these minutes, you'd agree with me that he could not be using the term "Joint Command" loosely as you said it was being used?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's true, but I think that it was not a Joint Command. Even though he used that term, it does not pertain to some sort of a command; it pertains to co-ordination between the entities that were to act there. A command needs to have certain attributes, certain duties. There has to be everything that is needed for a command. It is a generally accepted term for the co-ordination that existed between the forces that were active there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Mr. Djordjevic, I have to say that we are going a little bit slower than I was anticipating, so I'm going to ask you again to just focus on the questions and answer them directly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm going to have to ask you, Mr. Stamp, to continue at 20 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have reached our tape time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can we have a look at P902.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And while the document comes up, may I ask you, Mr. Djordjevic, you said - and we're moving on to Racak - you said that the minister ordered you to go down there to assist if you needed. What sort of assistance did you contemplate you could give?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That event caused great concern, both with the minister and with the entire leadership of Serbia. The minister wanted to gather information as quickly as possible and to make available information that would clarify this event. The accusations that were uttered by Walker at the press conference -- the minister wanted to neutralise that to some extent. We actually wanted to see what had happened there. So the minister issued an order for me to go there. I went there and I stayed there on the 17th in the afternoon and on the 18th until the members of the police came in and enabled the on-site investigation team to do their job.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So it sounds to me that you went down there basically on a fact-finding mission?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how I – how was I supposed to establish facts. My task was to assist the staff down there to, first of all, conduct an on-site investigation and that is the basic activity that is the starting point for establishing facts, to make it accessible to judicial organs, and then to see the whole course of events. It wasn’t my task to analyse the entire event from the beginning until the end. My task was only regarding the first part of the job which had to do with making it possible for the on-site investigation team to do its job on the ground and I was sent to do this task and I attended the execution of this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, what did you do actually? How did you assist them to do that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said that the overall situation caused great concern among the leadership of Serbia. The minister wanted to also have me there in addition to the staff which was operationally in charge of those tasks, so that I could be of assistance to the staff and for this job of facilitating the on-site investigation to be done properly. Well, that was the task and my assistance to the staff basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you leave on the 18th or on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received an order on the 17th at around lunchtime. The minister gave me the order to go down there, and then General Lukic after about an hour sent a helicopter to fetch me, and on the 17th in the afternoon I arrived at the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Maybe I'm not asking the question. I just want to move quickly. I just want to know: When did you leave Racak, what day -- not Racak, I mean Stimlje police station?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived at the police station on the 18th in the morning hours. It could have been 9.00 or 10.00 in the morning --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When did you leave?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From there I left once the on-site investigation team reached the mosque where the bodies were. So the minute they were able to conduct an on-site investigation and once that territory was under the police control, I returned to the staff. So it could have been sometime around 1300 hours. So on the 18th I left the police station in Stimlje, and I arrived in Pristina sometime around 1300 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Had an on-site investigation been conducted and completed by 1300 hours on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be certain that the investigation was concluded by that time. What was important for me was that the on-site investigation team arrived in the area and that they were able to conduct an on-site investigation. The minute they approached the mosque which was near the police station, my presence was no longer necessary and I returned back to Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So you left when they approached the mosque? You have answered that. Sorry. I withdraw that question. So you were told, according to your previous evidence, everything that had occurred during the police operation in detail by the staff. Can you tell us which units were involved in the operation?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember now, I think that a company of PJP unit from Urosevac participated in it and also some members of the operational pursuit groups also took part, but I'm not absolutely certain about that. I think that these were the forces that took part in the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How many men? How many men approximately? I know you won't recall exactly how many men.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The company had 90-odd men, and perhaps additional 30 to 40 from elsewhere. So 130 men, but I'm -- don't know exactly where they were from.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What was Goran Radosavljevic's role?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at that time he participated together with the members of the operational pursuit group in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was he the commander of that group, the OPGs?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He was a member of the staff. And as a member of the staff he took part in that operation. At that time, in the establishment sense, he wasn't a commander of that unit. There was approximately one squad each from the company and from the 124th Brigade. They had their own squad leaders, but Goran Radosavljevic took part in that operation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did the VJ participate?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that the army participated. I know that they had regularly deployed units in the area. They had camps in the vicinity of Stimlje, but I don't think that they took active part in the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Why is it you left only when the team approached the mosque, yet your responsibility was to ensure that the team, the on-site team, conducted the on-site investigation appropriately?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't tell you that nor was that my task --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Stop a minute there --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I went there --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please stop. I just want to be sure that I'm not misquoting you, because I recall after asking you two or three times you provided the answer, and this is at page 58, line 3 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After about my third question as to what you were supposed to be doing down there I suggested to you that you were on a fact-finding mission and you said: "I don't know how I was supposed to establish the facts." And you said: "My task was to assist the staff down there, first of all, to conduct an on-site investigation." And then at page 58, line 1, you said: "I was there to assist the police members in enabling the investigative team to conduct an on-site investigation and I did that." All I'm asking -- that is what you said?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not at all of what I said. Not a line of what you said is what I had said. I don't know how they do interpretation here, but that is definitely not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, you said it twice according to this. Okay. We'll check that. I'll ask you again then. What were you supposed to be doing down there?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, given what the situation was, namely, that after the intervention this territory where the event took place fell under the control of KLA, and given that Walker gave a press conference claiming that a massacre had been committed there, a crime, and so on, there were two or three attempts and then on the 15th, 16th, and even 17th, the on-site investigation team attempted to conduct an on-site investigation. They attempted to establish in a professional manner what had happened there. It wasn't possible to do that because the area was under the control of the KLA. The political tensions and concern among all entities, including the international community and Serbia, was great. The minister was expected to enable the judicial organs to conduct an on-site investigation and to see what the situation was on the ground, whether there were any casualties, and so on, to establish everything that an on-site investigation is supposed to establish. The minister issued an order to the staff for the staff to draft a plan on yet another attempt to enter the village to see whether there were any bodies of the people who had been killed in the village and to see what the situation was. All of this took place until the 17th when the minister issued an order for me to go down there as well. My task, given the seriousness of this situation, was to be present there and to provide assistance should it be needed. In accordance with that order, once I arrived there on the 17th in the afternoon, upon familiarising myself with these matters that I just described to you, I believed that it was necessary for me to go directly to Stimlje and to see how this operation that had been planned before my arrival was being conducted. I went on the following morning to Stimlje, and I was present there until the moment when there were all the necessary preconditions for the investigation team to come to the area where the operation was conducted. The moment they were able to do that, the moment it became possible for the investigation team to do that, given that the entire territory was at that point in time under the police control, I realised that my presence there was no longer necessary and I returned to Pristina. All the professional and expert measures that needed to be conducted with regard to the on-site investigation was done by the judicial investigations team. I wasn't there to effect were to exert any influence on their work. My role there was to ensure that all the preconditions were met for them to carry out their on-site investigation. Once I ascertained that it was possible for them to do that, I returned back, first to Pristina and then shortly thereafter to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So at the time you left, all you knew up until then is that they had arrived at the mosque; is that so?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question. I don't understand it. I don't want to have any misunderstandings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you left, when you left, your information was that they had arrived at the mosque, the team, the investigating team?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when the police put under the control the territory --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- where the operation had been conducted -- but please, I have to explain, to clear things up. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you left where was the team? Were they arriving at the mosque? Is that what you know when you left?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the police entered the mosque, found the bodies of the victims - they were lined up in the mosque - reported to the SUP chief who was there, right next to me. And the on-site investigation team that was already there -- that was also there, the on-site investigation team was told that they could go and carry out the on-site investigation. They left. Some 15 minutes later they reached the mosque. The police was already there. So at that time we knew that there were some 40 bodies in the mosque because the police when they entered the mosque saw that. And they informed the SUP chief, and he in turn --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- reported or informed the staff head about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, as far as that operation is concerned, was it only in the mosque that bodies were found?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the bodies were in the mosque. As they said at the time, they were lined up and the investigative judge confirmed that in his report following the on-site investigation. Those were the bodies that were found there. Now, whether there were other bodies too, it's a different issue. There was some information to the effect that there were some other bodies there that had been buried by the KLA previously because those were the bodies of their prominent fighters. That was some information that reached us, but I cannot really say it was a fact. The only bodies that were found were those in the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At the time of your presence down there in Kosovo and on the 17th and 18th in Pristina and Racak, do you know if the Joint Command was still operational? Was it still in existence and functioning?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The document in front of you is the record of a meeting of the collegium of the Chief of Staff of the -- of VJ with all the commanders, including the Chief of the General Staff present. It's P902. And the date is the 21st of January. If we move to page 11 of this -- of these minutes -- sorry, page 9. Let's go to page 9 first in English, which is page 7 in B/C/S. I'm going to move very quickly. General Dimitrijevic was in charge of supreme -- sorry, security administration for the army. In the middle of this passage where he's speaking he speaks of: "The OSCE Kosovo Verification Mission has been coming up with elements of the participation by the army." And he goes on to ask questions about whether or not the army participated in the event. If we go to the last line: " ... on the 16th of January in the morning ... where the MUP had carried out a mopping-up operation in Racak village and ... there was some 60-something killed." And if we could move to page 11 in the English, page 10 in the B/C/S -- top of page 10 in the B/C/S. And the bottom of page 11 in the English. And the Chief of the General Staff in these minutes address the inquiry. The second paragraph he said: "If the forces have to be used, nobody is denying that right of those who have the right to order it, but that means that if this joint staff, command, or whatever decided that the operation in Racak ... could not be carried out without the assistance of the Yugoslav Army, we know very well who must be asked for approval, if the FRY President orders, in spite of all the risk, that the Army be used, this decision must be carried out but bearing in mind the restrictions contained in the agreement, neither Pavkovic nor I have that right ..." The Chief of Staff is referring to the use or to the engagement of the army in the Racak operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you have a specific question, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I withdraw the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You withdraw. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if the counsel is withdrawing the statement then I don't have an objection, but I think there was a switch here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yeah, the general says if this joint staff, command, or whatever decided the operation in Racak could not be carried out without the assistance of the army, can you -- or do you know what information the general would have about the existence -- the continued existence of the Joint Command at this stage?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the first time I see this document. You started with General Aco Dimitrijevic. In his intervention he speaks about the 16th of January, saying that the mop-up operation was carried out and there was some 60 people who were killed. But that's not true. The operation was conducted on the 15th, and on the 15th and the 16th and the 17th the figure was not known. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- now whether the army took part and in what way, I didn't know that at the time. I didn't have any information to that effect in the field. We have heard various testimonies here, but this is the first time that I see this kind of discussion at the General Staff. To the extent of my knowledge at the time, the Yugoslav Army did not take part in the operation. It was present in the area, but I think that -- well, I didn't have any information that it used any of its assets. That's based on the information that I had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But, the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army is also referring to the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like us to go back to page 9 in the Serbian version so that we can see who is actually saying this. Where does it say that this is the Chief of the General Staff? I really don't see whether it is a Chief of the General Staff. I think that there is a mistake here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's under the heading Colonel-General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Serbian version, Your Honour, that's not what we're seeing, because the Serbian version is not on that page. Could we please have the page where we can see that this is General Ojdanic --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- but in the Serbian language because we see only the text because there is not a single name here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we on the Serbian version look at the bottom of the preceding page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who is that do you read there?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dragoljub Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Colonel-general?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel-General Dragoljub Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And let's get back to what he said on the next page. All I'm asking: He refers to the existence of the Joint Command and their possible involvement in this operation. Now, you were attending Joint Command meetings and you were down there at the time when this operation occurred, you were on the spot. My question is this: Do you know what facts the general would have to cause him to believe that the Joint Command was still functional?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are drawing conclusions that are invalid. First of all, I was not a member of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- please, I was not a member of the Joint Command, and I did not attend the meetings of the Joint Command. On that day I went to the MUP staff and I discussed this issue with General Sreten Lukic. I did not attend the meetings and I don't know whether they were held at the time and I don't know what the situation was. I had a specific task. I described to you -- for you what my task was, and when I completed it, on the orders of the minister, I went back to Belgrade --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Now --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and during my stay here on the 17th, in the evening, I did not attend any meetings except that one meeting with the head of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know why the general used language indicating that this staff or Joint Command continue to function?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at this area the MUP staff for the prevention of terrorism still existed. The Pristina Corps was still there. Both the Pristina Corps and the MUP staff were duty-bound in light of the delicacy of the situation to have a certain co-ordination, to co-ordinate their activities. I don't know how else I can explain this and how to try and get into the head of the Chief of the General Staff and to know what he meant when he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we have a look at P1052. And I suppose, Your Honours, it might be a convenient time because I'm moving on to an entirely new topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have checked. Could we please look at page 1 of this document in the Serbian version so that we can see the date of this document. At the bottom of the page, Your Honour, you can see that this is the collegium of the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army of the 24th of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you look at the previous page, the cover page, you see it says on the 21st of January, 1999 --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let me ask you a question, Mr. Djordjevic. How could the general be discussing the Racak operation in December 1998? Is that possible? Or please don't answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could just address this. The document seems to be a standard printed form with a date the 24th of December, 1998, appearing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Which document is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is the document P902, which is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that is showing a date of the 21st of --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: January --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- January 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Oh, it now becomes clear to me. I think in the copy in B/C/S we are missing the first page, so counsel didn't apparently get that first page. I think we have to correct that and put the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll hear from Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know what's on the first page of the B/C/S because I don't have it, but if you scroll down the BH -- B/C/S version, at the bottom of the page it says the collegium of the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, the 24th of December, 1998. The original is in B/C/S, so we see here that this is the collegium of the 24th of December, 1998. There could not have been any mistake there, and I think that we should clear this up, to get to the bottom of it. But when this was first placed on the screen it appeared to me that I saw the date the 24th of December, 1998, but then we moved on to another page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you look at the English version, it has the same date at the bottom, 24 December 1998. The subject matter of the passages of the transcript to which the witness has been referred appears clearly to be discussing events that occurred in January 1999 unless there were two such events with very similar circumstances if you look at what is said. This is a matter which we can't pursue further tonight because we've gone past 7.00, but we will continue the hearing tomorrow at 2.15. If there is any further substantive matter to be raised, it can be raised then. If the issue is simply that the date at the foot shows 24 December 1998 and the minutes on the first page suggest 21 December 1999, the Chamber is -- 21st of January, 1999, the Chamber is aware of that discrepancy and will have to give it consideration. If there are further facts relevant to the date that need to be brought out, they can be brought out tomorrow when we resume at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- may I quickly ask permission if I may correct the B/C/S version by putting the cover page, the first page, there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may. And I suggest you make a copy available to Mr. Djurdjic overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now and resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 10th day of December, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.
